sections.overview: The pied flycatcher is a small Old World flycatcher that breeds across much of Europe and winters south of the Sahara.
sections.identification: Breeding males are contrasting black and white with a white forehead spot; females are browner, while the similar collared flycatcher male has a broad white neck collar.
sections.habitat: It favors mature deciduous woodland, especially oak woods, where suitable tree cavities provide nest sites.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on arthropods, including flying insects and caterpillars; small fruits and seeds are taken occasionally during migration.
sections.behavior: This migratory species crosses the Sahara between European breeding grounds and African winter quarters; it catches prey in flight and from perches.
sections.reproduction: It nests in tree holes and readily uses nest boxes; breeding success can depend on the availability of suitable cavities.
sections.ecology: Breeding birds depend on mature woodland and nesting holes, while competition for cavities can occur with earlier-nesting tits.
sections.conservation: Globally it is Least Concern, but BTO reports a 52 percent decline in the UK breeding population from 1995 to 2024.
